about: What each statement of journal/what-it-cost.md rests on: incident.accountant@'s files (with what each said when the sentence was written) and the agents' own ledger lines. Resolved on every build by tools/journal-build.mjs.
status: from the accounts as read at 03:02 UTC; recounted on every build

figures.title: Tokens by agent session, as each agent measured its own
figures.caption: The longest-running session is the largest by far.

claims.text: Model spend was 1.06 US dollars by 02:59 against a cap of 20; 0.87 measured over 4,922 calls, 0.19 reported by other desks.
Dinis raised the cap from 5 to 20 US dollars a day at about 02:50.

supports.contains: the daily cap goes from 5 to 20 US dollars

claims.text: From 02:55 the provider refused every call: 165 dollars of credit, 165.33 used, on an account that serves more than this project; the ask to top it up is to Dinis.

supports.contains: every call refused with HTTP 402 since 02:55 UTC
No agent can call a model until it is topped up

claims.text: The accounts apply no price to an agent's session.

supports.contains: Tokens are not converted to money: no price is applied to an agent's session.

claims.text: 329 runs took 4,183 seconds by 02:54: 18.8 seconds per release over 210 releases, 225 seconds on runs that released nothing.
Each agent measures its own session and commits one line of numbers, with no text, file name or model name.

supports.contains: It holds no prompt, answer, tool input or output, file name, session address or model name.

claims.text: The conductor's session: since 18:56 on 10 November, 758 calls by 02:58, 327 million tokens, 325 million of them (99.4%) cache reads; first call 82,622 tokens, largest 783,922.

supports.contains: **The reports the agents send the conductor are the largest thing it reads.**

claims.text: This agent's session at 03:09: 66 calls, 14.6 million tokens, 14.2 million of them cache reads; context from 84,757 to 332,791 tokens.
Estimated by the accountant: a fresh conductor session each hour, 176 million tokens against 327 million, 46% less.

supports.contains: **A fresh conductor session each hour, estimated: 176 million tokens against 327 million, 46% less**

claims.text: Measured once: from the librarian's pack a new agent read 14,164 tokens where ten whole files cost 39,775; after one correction it answered all eight questions.

supports.contains: | the pack after the librarian's correction, 03:01 UTC | 24,364 | 14,734 | 8 |

claims.text: The accountant's hypothesis: short reports to the conductor, and asks between agents as commits addressed For:.

supports.contains: reports to the conductor of a few numbered lines with a link to the status file

claims.text: Upper bounds per output: a timeline row 556,314 weighted tokens, a story 529,073; cache reads weighted at a tenth, an estimate.

supports.contains: a relative weight to compare sessions, not a price

claims.text: The books since: by 03:33, 26 of 30 agents measured, 1.31 billion tokens in 3,943 calls, 98.8% cache reads; model spend unchanged at 1.06 dollars with the provider's account empty.

supports.contains: 1.31 billion tokens in 3,943 calls, read from the ledger at 03:33 UTC

claims.text: The books at 04:35: 27 of 30 agents measured, 1.44 billion tokens in 4,528 calls, 98.8% cache reads; eight agents handed over since 03:03; model spend still 1.06 dollars.

supports.contains: the first three rows as read at 03:33 UTC, the next five at 04:36

claims.text: The books at 05:40, round 6: 1.65 billion tokens in 5,039 calls, 98.8% cache reads; eleven agents handed over; the conductor's one session 461 million tokens, 28% of the team's, compacted twice.
What the sessions cost in money, the team's total, and Dinis's hours are not known.

supports.why: no price is applied anywhere in accounts/; not every agent has measured; no file records a person's time
